text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 0.45% today, continuing a slide from its peak of $478 six trading days ago. The stock has lost nearly $21 per share in just over a week despite crude oil prices hitting six-month highs — Brent is now above $116 per barrel. This disconnect points to the market pricing in a real risk: while high oil prices can boost refinery margins in theory, geopolitical escalation in the Middle East (U.S. strikes on Iran, Houthi attacks, American diplomats pulled from Saudi Arabia) threatens to disrupt global supply chains and create uncertainty that outweighs the short-term benefit of elevated crude costs.

U.S. refineries are running at 93.4% capacity with healthy fuel inventories, so the company isn't constrained by supply or demand on the domestic side. The sell-off appears driven by worry that a widening regional conflict could destabilize energy markets in ways that hurt refiner operations — whether through logistics disruptions, financial market volatility, or a shift in how crude flows globally — rather than by any weakness in the refining business itself right now.
